meta.title: The New Student
meta.blurb: Aoife has just arrived from Ireland, and Kaio has to be her buddy. Will she feel at home in Brazil, or will she want to go back? It depends on you.

p1.title: The Girl from Galway
text: On the first Monday of August, Professor Marcos, the coordinator, was waiting for Kaio at the school gate. “You speak the best English in your class,” he said. “Would you like to be the [[buddy|parceiro de apoio]] of our new [[exchange student|aluna de intercâmbio]]?”
Before Kaio could answer, a tall girl with red hair got out of a car. She was carrying a huge backpack, and she looked a little [[lost|perdida]].

“Hi! I'm Aoife,” she said with a smile. “It's pronounced EE-fa. Don't worry, nobody gets it right the first time.” She was from Galway, a city on the west coast of Ireland, and she was [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] study at IFAL for one semester.
In the classroom, thirty students [[stared|ficaram olhando fixamente]] at her. Then the teacher turned to Kaio. “Kaio, can you introduce our visitor?”
Kaio felt his face getting hot. Aoife knew only three words in Portuguese: obrigada, bom dia and tapioca.

p2a.title: Twenty Questions
text: Kaio introduced Aoife in English and translated everything. Soon, the whole class was asking her questions.

“Have you ever eaten tapioca?” asked Júlia. “Not yet,” said Aoife, “but I've already heard a lot about it!” “Have you ever seen snow?” asked someone else. “Yes, a few times,” she laughed, “but I've never seen a beach as warm as yours.”
Then Aoife turned to Kaio. “And you? Have you ever been [[abroad|no exterior]]?” Kaio shook his head. “I've never left Alagoas,” he admitted.

At lunch, however, something happened. While Aoife was waiting in line, Tiago, the [[class clown|palhaço da turma]], started to imitate her [[accent|sotaque]]: “Hi! I'm from Ai-er-land!” A few students laughed. Aoife [[pretended|fingiu]] not to hear, but her [[cheeks|bochechas]] turned red.
After that, Tiago looked at Kaio, waiting for him to laugh too.

p2b.title: Portuguese, Please
text: “Try in Portuguese,” Kaio [[whispered|sussurrou]]. “Everybody will love it.” First, Aoife looked at the class. Then she took a deep breath.

“Bom dia. Eu... chamar... Aoife. Eu... ser... da Irlanda,” she said slowly. For a moment, nobody said anything. Then Tiago, the [[class clown|palhaço da turma]], repeated her words with a funny voice, and half of the class laughed.
Aoife smiled, but her hands were [[shaking|tremendo]]. She sat down and didn't speak for the rest of the morning.
At the end of the day, she found Kaio at the bus stop. “I've studied Portuguese for three months,” she said quietly, in English. “And I've never felt so stupid in my life.”

p3x.title: A Deal

text.text: Tiago rolled his eyes when Kaio told him to stop, but he never imitated Aoife again. That afternoon, Aoife thanked Kaio. “Nobody has ever defended me like that,” she said.
“Everybody feels stupid when they're learning a language,” Kaio told her. “I felt the same when I started English. Let's practice together.”

text: So they made a [[deal|acordo]]: every day after lunch, she taught him Irish expressions and he taught her Portuguese. In two weeks, Aoife was saying “oxente” like a real alagoana, and Kaio had learned that “grand” means “OK” in Ireland.
Later, on a Friday afternoon, Aoife asked: “What do people here do on weekends? I've been here for three weeks, and I haven't seen anything outside the school yet.”
Kaio thought about it. His grandmother was going to the town festival on Saturday. But there was also the big shopping mall in Maceió, and Aoife probably missed things from home.

p3y.title: The Video
text: Kaio laughed. It was just a joke, he thought. Tiago was always joking with everybody.
But that night, Tiago posted a video of his imitation in the class group chat. By the morning, it had more than three hundred views, and people from other classes were repeating it in the corridors.
Aoife didn't say anything. However, she started eating lunch alone, with her headphones on. When Kaio sat next to her, she answered with short sentences: “Yes.” “No.” “I'm fine.”

On Thursday, Júlia [[pulled Kaio aside|chamou o Kaio num canto]]. “She saw you laughing, you know,” she said. “I think she's really hurt. Have you talked to her since Monday?” Kaio realized that he hadn't.

p3z.title: Silence
text: “So... do you like the food here?” Kaio asked, and the moment passed. Aoife answered politely, but she never tried to speak Portuguese in class again.

In the following weeks, she spent most of her [[breaks|intervalos]] on video calls with her mother. When the teachers asked her something, she answered in English, and after a while, the class stopped trying to talk to her.
One day, Kaio heard her on the phone near the library. Her voice was [[trembling|trêmula]]. “Mam, I've been here for a month, and I haven't made a single friend.”
Kaio stopped walking. Was that partly his fault?

p4a.title: The Festival
text: On Saturday night, the town square was full of lights, music and the smell of corn. Kaio's grandmother, Vó Neide, took Aoife by the hand and taught her to dance forró. After ten minutes, Aoife was laughing so much that she could hardly breathe.

Later, a man started playing a fast song on the [[accordion|sanfona]]. Suddenly, Aoife stopped. “This sounds a bit like Irish music!” she said, and she showed them a few steps of an Irish dance. A small crowd [[gathered|se juntou]] around them and clapped.
On the way home, Aoife was quiet for a while. Then she said: “The program has asked me if I want to stay for another semester. I have to decide by Friday. What do you think?”

p4b.title: The Invitation

text.text: At the mall, Aoife looked around politely. “It's... exactly like the malls at home,” she said. She bought a keychain, and they took the bus back. It was a nice day, but not a special one.
Kaio apologized. “I shouldn't have laughed,” he said. Aoife accepted his apology, but after that, she was more careful with him.

text: Then the weeks went by, and Aoife's Portuguese was getting better, although she still made funny mistakes.

Finally, near the end of the semester, Professor Marcos invited her to give a short presentation about Ireland to the whole school, in Portuguese. “I've never spoken in front of so many people,” she told Kaio. “And in Portuguese! Will you help me prepare it?”
Kaio [[hesitated|hesitou]]. He had two tests that week and a project for his programming class.

p4c.title: Too Late?
text: Kaio decided not to do anything. After all, Aoife was only [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] stay for one semester.

text.text: Meanwhile, Tiago's video kept [[circulating|circulando]]. Someone made a sticker with Aoife's face, and it appeared in every group chat at school.

text: Aoife became quieter every week. She stopped coming to school events, and she sat alone at the back of the classroom.

One Monday, her desk was empty. Later, Kaio saw Professor Marcos in the corridor and asked about her. “She's thinking about going home early,” he said. “She has told me that she's very unhappy here. Do you know why?”

p4d.title: Study Group
text: Kaio invited Aoife to study with Júlia and two other friends in the library. At first, she was shy. However, when Júlia asked for help with an English exercise, Aoife explained it so clearly that everybody applauded.

After that, the study group became a daily [[meeting|encontro]]. They helped her with Portuguese, she helped them with English, and they asked each other [[endless|sem fim]] questions: “Have you ever eaten jaca?” “Have you ever tried Irish soda bread?”
Later, one afternoon, Aoife looked at the group and smiled. “You know, I almost went home early last month,” she said. “I'm really glad I didn't.”

e1.title: Best Friends
text: Aoife decided to stay for another semester. When she told the class, everybody [[cheered|comemorou]], even Tiago.

Later, in December, she flew to Galway for Christmas. However, she came back in February with a [[suitcase|mala]] full of Irish chocolates and a surprise for Kaio: an invitation from her family to visit Ireland one day.
“You've never been abroad,” she said, “so our house will be your first stop.” Kaio laughed. He had never imagined that being a buddy would change his life.

e2.title: The Culture Swap
text: On the last Friday of the semester, the school held its first Culture Afternoon. Kaio's classmates played forró, and Aoife taught everybody a simple Irish dance. There was tapioca on one table and Irish soda bread on the other.
More than two hundred students came. Even Tiago danced, badly but with enthusiasm.
When Aoife went home in December, she left a note on Kaio's desk: “You've shown me the real Brazil. Next time, I'll show you the real Ireland.”

e3.title: A Polite Goodbye
text: The semester ended quietly. On her last day, Aoife hugged some classmates and thanked Kaio for his help.
“You've been very kind,” she said. It was true, but it sounded like something people say to a neighbor, not to a friend.

A few weeks later, Kaio looked at her profile online. There were photos of Galway, her friends and the sea. Suddenly, he realized that they had never really talked about anything important. He had been her buddy, but never her friend.

e4.title: Lost in Translation
text: Kaio and Aoife worked on the presentation for a week. On the big day, the auditorium was full, and Aoife spoke in Portuguese for ten minutes. First, she talked about Galway. Then she described the rain and the green hills. Everything was going well.

At the end, she wanted to thank the school for the delicious food. Instead of saying “Estou satisfeita,” she said proudly: “Estou cheia de vocês!” The auditorium went silent for a second, and then everybody [[burst out laughing|caiu na gargalhada]].

Aoife didn't understand, so Kaio explained: in Portuguese, her sentence also meant “I'm fed up with you all.” She laughed so hard that she cried. For the rest of the semester, “Estou cheia!” was the school's favorite joke, and Aoife never forgot the difference.

e5.title: Early Flight
text: Two weeks later, Aoife went back to Ireland, three months before the end of the semester.
Professor Marcos read her message to the class: “Thank you for everything. I've learned a lot in Brazil, but I've felt very alone here. I hope the next exchange student has a better experience.”
Kaio looked at the empty desk. He hadn't done anything wrong, he thought. But he hadn't done anything right, either.

question.q: Why did Aoife go home early?
options: She got a job in Ireland

e6.title: Just a Joke
text: Aoife went home three months early. Before she left, she sent one message to the class group. It was a screenshot of Tiago's video, with a short sentence: “It was never just a joke for me.”
Nobody answered. Tiago deleted the video that night, but it was too late.
Kaio remembered the first lunch, when Tiago was looking at him, waiting for him to laugh. One different reaction could have changed everything. Finally, he understood that.
